html:
SMTO-API-0016 — SMTO couldn't find the result of that request

GUID: e663062b-903e-4b32-881a-a53f591ab376
Slug: integration-result-not-found
Domain: API · Subsystem: api

What happened

  • A program connected to SMTO asked for the result of an earlier request, but SMTO has no saved result under that request ID. The ID may be wrong, or the result may have been deleted.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check that the program or script uses the exact request ID SMTO gave back when the request was sent, and that it connects to the same SMTO. A result can only be found with its own ID, on the SMTO that ran it.
  2. Open SMTO in your browser and look in the conversation list for the conversation that request created. If it's there, the work ran and you can read its outcome directly.
  3. If the conversation is gone, check whether Auto-purge is turned on in Settings › Data. Auto-purge permanently deletes inactive conversations, and a deleted request's result can't be fetched.
  4. Only after confirming the earlier request didn't do the work, send it again from the program. Sending it again when it already ran would do the same work twice.

What success looks like

  • The program gets the result for its request ID, or you have confirmed in SMTO what that request did.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details, or copy the error from the program's output, and send it with the request ID to the person who manages SMTO. Don't swap in a different request's ID to get an answer; that result belongs to other work.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The integration results endpoint found no trace for the requested request_id (trace lookup returned nothing or the event wait raised KeyError) and returned HTTP 404.

What this means

  • Integration result lookup finds no retained trace or waiting for its result raises a missing-identity lookup. Generic API status and exception families establish only their stated boundary. Stronger structured causes take precedence; the original receipt determines whether work started or had effects, and diagnostics add no dispatch or retry.

Why this can happen

  • Integration result lookup finds no retained trace or waiting for its result raises a missing-identity lookup.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the original integration request ID with retained traces; missing result is not proof of no execution.

How to fix it

  • Verify the client uses the request_id returned by /api/agent/integrations/execute (or the child request_id returned by confirm/clarify) against the same Server. If the trace was purged or its conversation deleted, inspect the conversation and task state to establish what ran before resubmitting; do not substitute another request's ID.
  • Refresh the integration’s retained results and use an existing result identity.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The original retained result is located or its operation state is reconciled.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • Generic API status and exception families establish only their stated boundary. Stronger structured causes take precedence; the original receipt determines whether work started or had effects, and diagnostics add no dispatch or retry.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
